objectives.description: Identify and apply the elements of art (line, shape, colour, texture, form, space) and principles of design
Demonstrate observational drawing and shading techniques using natural objects and still life
Apply painting techniques including watercolour and tempera to create original works of art
Produce craftwork using local materials including weaving, tie-dye, and textile design
Explain the importance of the arts to Nigerian society and cultural identity
Identify the fundamentals of music including musical alphabet, clef, staves, notes, and their relative values
Demonstrate ear training by identifying pitch, intervals, and harmony in musical passages
Sing the solfa notes of the Nigerian National Anthem and practise major scales
Identify types of singing voices and use breathing exercises for voice training
Describe traditional Nigerian music styles and their cultural contexts
Play a simple recorder or other classroom instrument applying learned musical principles
Describe the origin, forms, and elements of drama and theatre and identify people involved in theatre production
Explain the roles and duties of a theatre director in coordinating stage productions
Identify the functions and areas of theatre design including costumes, lighting, and set design
Perform improvisation and dramatise scenes from recommended texts or original scripts
Describe career opportunities in drama and identify notable Nigerian dramatists and playwrights
Describe the rehearsal process and participate in structured school drama productions
Identify types of dance including traditional, modern, and creative dance forms practised in Nigeria
Describe the role of a choreographer and demonstrate basic processes of choreography in creating a dance pattern
Identify career prospects in dance and name notable Nigerian dance artists and companies
Perform elements of traditional Nigerian dance styles as part of cultural appreciation
